attributes.description: Name of the column that serves as the unique business key for members at this level. Used for joining and identifying dimension members in star schema queries.

attributes.name: level_name
attributes.description: Name of the hierarchical level within the dimension. Examples: 'Country', 'Region', 'Market', 'District', 'Cell Site' for geography; 'Product Line', 'Product Family', 'Product Category', 'Product Subcategory', 'Stock Keeping Unit (SKU)' for product.

attributes.name: level_name_column
attributes.description: Name of the column that contains the human-readable display name for members at this level. Used for report labels and user interface presentation.

attributes.name: level_ordinal_position
attributes.description: Numeric position of this level within the hierarchy, starting from 1 at the top (most aggregated) level. Determines drill-down sequence and roll-up aggregation order in OLAP operations.

attributes.name: olap_cube_name
attributes.description: Name of the Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) cube or analytical model that uses this hierarchy. Links the hierarchy definition to deployed Business Intelligence (BI) assets.

attributes.name: parent_level_name
attributes.description: Name of the immediate parent level in the hierarchy. Null for the top-most level. Defines the parent-child relationship for roll-up aggregations.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or data product that provides the hierarchy definition. Examples: 'Netcracker Product Catalog', 'Salesforce CRM', 'SAP S/4HANA Master Data'.

attributes.name: supports_drill_down
attributes.description: Indicates whether this hierarchy supports drill-down navigation from aggregated to detailed levels in Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) operations.

attributes.name: supports_roll_up
attributes.description: Indicates whether this hierarchy supports roll-up aggregation from detailed to summary levels in Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) operations.

attributes.name: usage_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing guidance on proper usage of this hierarchy, including business rules, calculation logic, and known limitations. Supports self-service analytics.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the hierarchy definition. Incremented when hierarchy structure changes. Supports change tracking and historical comparison of hierarchy evolution.

attributes.name: parent_dimension_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on dimension_hierarchy (parent_dimension_hierarchy_id)

products.name: analytical_subject_area
products.description: Master registry of all analytical subject areas (data marts / analytical domains) defined within the telecommunications analytics platform — e.g., Network Analytics, Customer Analytics, Revenue Analytics, Usage Analytics, Workforce Analytics. Captures subject area name, owning business domain, primary grain, refresh cadence, platform layer (Silver/Gold), responsible data product owner, and associated KPI families. Serves as the top-level organizational taxonomy for the analytics catalog and governs which KPIs, dimensions, and data quality rules belong to each subject area.
products.reference: TM Forum IG1131 Analytics Subject Area

attributes.name: analytical_subject_area_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the analytical subject area. Primary key.

attributes.name: data_product_owner_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Product Owner Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to people.employee. Business justification: Data product ownership is foundational to data mesh operating models in telecommunications. Owner accountability for SLA compliance, consumer support, and product roadmap decisions. Denormalized name/

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date when this analytical subject area was formally approved by the data governance council.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The governance approval status of this analytical subject area indicating whether it has been reviewed and approved by data governance council.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the data governance authority or individual who approved this analytical subject area for production use.

attributes.name: business_purpose
attributes.description: Detailed description of the business objectives, use cases, and analytical questions this subject area is designed to answer.

attributes.name: consumer_count
attributes.description: The number of distinct business users, teams, or downstream systems that consume data from this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: contains_pii_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this analytical subject area contains any personally identifiable information subject to privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, CPNI).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, CCPA, FCC CPNI Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this analytical subject area record was first created in the catalog.

attributes.name: data_classification_level
attributes.description: The highest data classification level of any data element within this subject area (public, internal, confidential, restricted), determining access controls and handling requirements.

attributes.name: data_quality_rule_count
attributes.description: The number of data quality rules, validation checks, or business rules applied to data within this subject area.

attributes.name: data_retention_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days that data in this analytical subject area is retained before archival or deletion, driven by regulatory, compliance, or business requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5, FCC Data Retention Rules

attributes.name: dimension_count
attributes.description: The number of analytical dimensions (e.g., time, geography, product, customer segment) associated with this subject area.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: The URL link to the detailed technical and business documentation for this analytical subject area, including data dictionary, lineage, and usage guidelines.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date when this analytical subject area was retired, deprecated, or replaced. Null if still active.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date when this analytical subject area became active and available for business use.

attributes.name: fact_table_count
attributes.description: The number of fact tables or measurement tables included within this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: kpi_family_count
attributes.description: The number of distinct KPI families or metric groups associated with this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this analytical subject area record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: last_refresh_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent data refresh or load operation for this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the analytical subject area indicating whether it is actively used, under development, deprecated, or retired.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special instructions, or contextual information about this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: owning_domain
attributes.description: The primary business domain responsible for this analytical subject area (e.g., Customer, Network, Billing, Product, Order, Service, Workforce, Partner, Usage, Revenue Assurance, Inventory, Interconnect, Content, Compliance, Enterprise). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: customer|network|billing|product|order|service|workforce|partner|usage|revenue_assurance|inventory|interconnect|content|compliance|enterprise — 15 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: TM Forum eTOM (Enhanced Telecom Operations Map)

attributes.name: platform_layer
attributes.description: The lakehouse medallion architecture layer where this subject area resides (Bronze for raw, Silver for cleansed/conformed, Gold for aggregated/business-ready, Platinum for advanced analytics).

attributes.name: primary_consumer_group
attributes.description: The primary business function or user group that consumes this analytical subject area (e.g., Network Operations, Finance, Marketing, Executive Leadership).
attributes.references: TM Forum eTOM (Enhanced Telecom Operations Map)

attributes.name: primary_grain
attributes.description: The fundamental level of detail or granularity at which data is stored in this subject area (e.g., per customer per day, per cell site per hour, per invoice line item).

attributes.name: primary_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the primary operational system of record that serves as the main data source for this analytical subject area (e.g., Amdocs Revenue Management, Salesforce CRM, Nokia NetAct).

attributes.name: refresh_cadence
attributes.description: The frequency at which data in this analytical subject area is refreshed or updated (real-time, near real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, on-demand). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: real_time|near_real_time|hourly|daily|weekly|monthly|on_demand — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: regulatory_scope
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of regulatory frameworks or compliance requirements applicable to this subject area (e.g., GDPR, FCC, CPNI, SOX, IFRS 15).

attributes.name: sla_availability_target_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Availability Target Percentage
attributes.description: The target availability percentage for this analytical subject area as defined in the SLA with business consumers (e.g., 99.9% uptime).

attributes.name: sla_refresh_target_minutes
attributes.description: The maximum allowable time in minutes between data refresh cycles to meet business SLA requirements for data freshness.

attributes.name: source_system_count
attributes.description: The number of distinct operational source systems (OSS/BSS) that contribute data to this analytical subject area.

attributes.name: subject_area_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the subject area for system integration and reporting (e.g., NET_ANLYT, CUST_ANLYT, REV_ANLYT).

attributes.name: subject_area_name
attributes.description: The business-friendly name of the analytical subject area (e.g., Network Analytics, Customer Analytics, Revenue Analytics, Usage Analytics, Workforce Analytics).

attributes.name: subject_area_type
attributes.description: Classification of the analytical subject area based on its primary business purpose (operational, strategic, regulatory, customer-facing, network performance, financial).

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of business tags or labels for categorization, search, and discovery of this analytical subject area (e.g., customer_360, network_performance, revenue_assurance).

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: The semantic version number of this analytical subject area schema (e.g., 1.0.0, 2.1.3) following major.minor.patch convention.

attributes.name: parent_analytical_subject_area_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on analytical_subject_area (parent_analytical_subject_area_id)

products.name: dq_rule
products.description: Master catalog of all Data Quality (DQ) rules defined across the telecommunications data platform — the SSOT for data quality governance definitions. Captures rule name, rule type (completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, timeliness, accuracy), rule expression or SQL predicate, severity level (critical, major, minor), target domain and product, expected threshold percentage, remediation guidance, and rule owner. Covers rules for CDR completeness, MSISDN format validity, billing amount non-negativity, SLA breach timeliness, and subscriber record uniqueness. Used by the DQ execution engine to validate Silver Layer data.
products.reference: DAMA DMBOK2 — Data Quality Rules

attributes.name: dq_rule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the data quality rule. Primary key for the DQ rule catalog.

attributes.name: rule_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to people.employee. Business justification: Data quality rule ownership enables accountability for rule maintenance, threshold adjustments, and false-positive resolution. Critical for DQ incident escalation workflows and rule approval processes

attributes.name: alert_channel
attributes.description: The communication channel used to notify stakeholders when this rule is violated beyond threshold. Multiple channels may be comma-separated.

attributes.name: alert_recipient_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses, Slack channels, or PagerDuty service keys that should receive alerts when this rule fails. Supports distribution lists and role-based aliases.

attributes.name: business_impact
attributes.description: Description of the business consequences if this rule is violated. Examples: revenue leakage, SLA breach, customer churn risk, regulatory penalty, network outage, billing dispute.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rule was first created in the DQ catalog. Immutable audit field.

attributes.name: data_lineage_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the data lineage graph or metadata catalog entry that shows the upstream sources and downstream consumers of the data validated by this rule. Used for impact analysis.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: Link to external documentation, wiki page, or knowledge base article that provides additional context, examples, or troubleshooting guidance for this rule.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date after which this rule version is no longer active. Null indicates the rule is currently in effect with no planned end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this rule version becomes active and should be applied to data. Used for temporal rule management and historical analysis.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: How often this rule should be executed by the DQ engine. Real-time rules run on streaming data, batch rules run on scheduled intervals, on-demand rules are triggered manually.

attributes.name: execution_layer
attributes.description: The lakehouse medallion architecture layer where this rule is executed. Bronze for raw data validation, Silver for cleansed data validation, Gold for aggregated/curated data validation.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rule is currently active and should be executed by the DQ engine. False means the rule is disabled (e.g., temporarily suspended during system maintenance or deprecated).

attributes.name: is_blocking
attributes.description: Indicates whether violations of this rule should block downstream processing. True means failed records are quarantined and not promoted to the next layer. False means violations are logged but processing continues.

attributes.name: last_execution_status
attributes.description: The outcome of the most recent execution of this rule. Success means the rule ran without errors, failure means execution failed, warning means execution succeeded but violations exceeded threshold, skipped means the rule was not executed due to conditions not being met.

attributes.name: last_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rule was last executed by the DQ engine. Used to monitor execution frequency and detect stale rules.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the person or system that last modified this rule. Used for audit and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rule was last updated. Updated whenever rule logic, thresholds, or metadata are changed.

attributes.name: last_pass_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of records that passed this rule during the last execution (0.00 to 100.00). Used to track data quality trends over time.

attributes.name: regulatory_mandate
attributes.description: Reference to the specific regulatory requirement, compliance framework, or industry standard that mandates this rule (e.g., FCC Part 64, GDPR Article 5, 3GPP TS 32.401). Null if the rule is business-driven rather than regulatory.

attributes.name: related_kpi
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the business KPI that depends on this data quality rule. Examples: ARPU accuracy, churn prediction reliability, SLA compliance rate, CDR completeness for billing.

attributes.name: remediation_guidance
attributes.description: Step-by-step instructions for data stewards on how to investigate and resolve violations of this rule. May include links to runbooks, contact information for data owners, or automated remediation procedures.

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Classification of the rule by its purpose. Structural rules validate schema and format, semantic rules check meaning and relationships, business rules enforce business logic, regulatory rules ensure compliance with FCC, GDPR, or other mandates.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code for the rule following pattern DOMAIN_TYPE_NUMBER (e.g., CDR_CMP_001, MSISDN_VAL_002). Used for programmatic reference and cross-system integration.

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of what the rule validates, why it matters, and the expected outcome. Provides context for business users and data stewards.

attributes.name: rule_expression
attributes.description: The logical expression or SQL predicate that defines the rule logic. May contain Spark SQL syntax, Python expressions, or declarative predicates. Example: 'msisdn IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(msisdn) = 10' or 'billing_amount >= 0'.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the data quality rule. Used for identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Category of data quality dimension this rule validates. Completeness checks for missing values, uniqueness ensures no duplicates, validity verifies format/range, consistency checks cross-field logic, timeliness measures freshness, accuracy validates correctness against source of truth.

attributes.name: rule_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the rule definition following major.minor.patch format (e.g., 1.0.0, 2.1.3). Incremented when rule logic, thresholds, or metadata are updated.

attributes.name: sample_violation_query
attributes.description: A SQL query template that data stewards can run to retrieve sample records that violate this rule. Used for investigation and root cause analysis.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Impact classification of rule violations. Critical failures block downstream processing, major issues require immediate remediation, minor issues are logged for review, warnings are informational only.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of user-defined tags for categorization and search. Examples: billing, network, customer-facing, regulatory, high-priority. Used for filtering and grouping rules in the DQ dashboard.

attributes.name: target_attribute
attributes.description: The specific column or attribute within the target product that this rule validates. Null if the rule applies to the entire record or multiple attributes.

attributes.name: target_domain
attributes.description: The business domain this rule applies to (e.g., Customer, Network, Billing, Product, Order, Service, Usage, Revenue Assurance). Aligns with the enterprise data domain taxonomy.

attributes.name: target_product
attributes.description: The specific data product or table this rule validates (e.g., cdr, subscriber, invoice, network_element). References the lakehouse Silver Layer product catalog.

attributes.name: technical_implementation
attributes.description: The technical framework or method used to implement this rule in the DQ execution engine. Spark SQL for native SQL predicates, Python UDF for custom logic, Great Expectations or Deequ for framework-based validation.
attributes.references: Apache Spark, Great Expectations, AWS Deequ

attributes.name: threshold_operator
attributes.description: The comparison operator used to evaluate the threshold. Typically '>=' for minimum pass rates, '<=' for maximum error rates.

attributes.name: threshold_percentage
attributes.description: The minimum acceptable pass rate for this rule as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Example: 99.50 means at least 99.5% of records must pass. Used to trigger alerts when quality falls below threshold.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the person or system that created this rule. Used for audit and accountability.

attributes.name: derived_from_dq_rule_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on dq_rule (derived_from_dq_rule_id)

products.name: dq_execution_result
products.description: Transactional record of each Data Quality rule execution run against a target data product in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Captures execution timestamp, rule reference, target domain and product, records evaluated count, records passed count, records failed count, pass rate percentage, execution status (passed, failed, warning), failure sample records (JSON), and triggering pipeline run ID. Provides the operational audit trail for data quality monitoring, SLA compliance for data freshness, and feeds the DQ dashboard for the data governance team.
products.reference: DAMA DMBOK2 — DQ Measurement

attributes.name: dq_execution_result_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each data quality rule execution result record. Primary key for the DQ execution result entity.

attributes.name: dq_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific data quality rule that was executed in this run. Links to the DQ rule catalog.

attributes.name: pipeline_run_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the Databricks pipeline or job run that triggered this data quality rule execution. Enables traceability to upstream data processing workflows.

attributes.name: business_date
attributes.description: Business effective date for which the data quality rule was executed. May differ from execution_timestamp for batch processing of historical data.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this execution result record was first created in the DQ execution result table. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: data_steward_notified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assigned data steward was notified of this rule execution result. True if notification was sent; false otherwise.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Detailed error or exception message if the rule execution encountered a technical failure (execution_status = error). Null for successful executions.

attributes.name: execution_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total time in seconds taken to execute the data quality rule against the target data product. Used for performance monitoring and optimization.

attributes.name: execution_mode
attributes.description: Mode in which the data quality rule was executed. Scheduled for automated runs; manual for ad-hoc validation; triggered for event-driven execution; continuous for streaming data validation.

attributes.name: execution_status
attributes.description: Overall outcome status of the data quality rule execution. Passed indicates all records met the rule criteria; failed indicates threshold breach; warning indicates approaching threshold; error indicates execution failure; skipped indicates rule was not applicable.

attributes.name: execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the data quality rule execution was initiated. Used for operational audit trail and SLA compliance tracking.

attributes.name: failure_sample_records
attributes.description: JSON array containing a sample of records that failed the data quality rule. Includes primary key and relevant attribute values to enable root cause analysis. Limited to first 100 failures for performance.

attributes.name: failure_threshold_percentage
attributes.description: Configured threshold percentage below which the rule execution is considered failed. Used to determine execution_status based on pass_rate_percentage.

attributes.name: pass_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of records that passed the data quality rule, calculated as (records_passed_count / records_evaluated_count) * 100. Key metric for DQ dashboard and SLA monitoring.

attributes.name: records_evaluated_count
attributes.description: Total number of records in the target data product that were evaluated against the data quality rule during this execution.

attributes.name: records_failed_count
attributes.description: Number of records that did not meet the data quality rule criteria. Used to calculate failure rate and identify data quality issues.

attributes.name: records_passed_count
attributes.description: Number of records that successfully met the data quality rule criteria. Used to calculate pass rate percentage.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Recommended or automated remediation action to address data quality failures (e.g., quarantine records, trigger data steward notification, auto-correct). Supports operational response workflows.

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Classification of the data quality rule based on ISO 25012 quality dimensions. Enables categorization of DQ issues for governance reporting.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Business-friendly code identifier for the executed rule (e.g., CUS-VAL-001 for customer validation rule 001). Enables human-readable rule reference in reports and dashboards.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the data quality rule that was executed (e.g., Customer Email Format Validation, MSISDN Length Check).

attributes.name: rule_severity
attributes.description: Business impact severity of the data quality rule. Critical rules block downstream processing; low severity rules are informational only.

attributes.name: rule_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the data quality rule definition at the time of execution. Enables tracking of rule changes over time and historical comparison.

attributes.name: sla_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this execution result meets the defined SLA for data quality. True if pass_rate_percentage meets or exceeds the SLA threshold; false if SLA is breached.

attributes.name: target_domain
attributes.description: Business domain of the data product being validated (e.g., Customer, Network, Billing, Product). Aligns with enterprise data domain taxonomy.

attributes.name: target_layer
attributes.description: Lakehouse medallion architecture layer where the target data product resides. Typically silver for curated business entities.

attributes.name: target_product
attributes.description: Name of the specific data product (table/entity) in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer that was evaluated by this rule execution.

attributes.name: warning_threshold_percentage
attributes.description: Configured threshold percentage below which the rule execution triggers a warning status. Enables proactive alerting before SLA breach.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or service account that created this execution result record. Typically the DQ framework service account for automated executions.

attributes.name: rerun_of_dq_execution_result_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Rerun Of Dq Execution Result Id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on dq_execution_result (rerun_of_dq_execution_result_id)

products.name: dq_issue
products.description: Operational record of a confirmed Data Quality issue identified through DQ rule execution or manual data steward review. Captures issue description, severity, affected domain and product, affected record count, root cause category (source system defect, ETL transformation error, schema change, business rule gap), assigned data steward, remediation action taken, resolution status, and SLA breach flag. Tracks the full lifecycle of a DQ issue from detection through remediation and closure. Distinct from dq_execution_result which is the raw measurement — this is the managed issue record.
products.reference: DAMA DMBOK2 — Data Issue Management

attributes.name: dq_issue_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the data quality issue record. Primary key for the DQ issue entity.

attributes.name: affected_network_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.element. Business justification: Data quality issues in network performance data must be traceable to specific network elements for root cause analysis and remediation. Network operations teams require DQ issue tracking tied to infra

attributes.name: dq_execution_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the specific DQ rule execution run that produced the measurement leading to this issue. Links the managed issue to the raw measurement event.

attributes.name: dq_rule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the DQ rule that detected this issue. Null if the issue was identified through manual data steward review.

attributes.name: location_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to location.location_site. Business justification: Data quality issues in network data are often traced to specific site equipment or collection points for remediation. Links DQ issues to physical infrastructure for field technician dispatch and equip

attributes.name: primary_dq_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the data steward responsible for investigating and remediating this DQ issue.

attributes.name: spare_part_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.spare_part. Business justification: Inventory data quality issues (stock discrepancies, obsolete records, missing BOMs) are logged as DQ issues to drive supply chain data stewardship and remediation workflows.

attributes.name: acknowledged_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the assigned data steward acknowledged receipt and ownership of the issue.

attributes.name: affected_attribute
attributes.description: The specific column or attribute within the data product that exhibits the quality defect. Null if the issue is record-level or cross-attribute.

attributes.name: affected_domain
attributes.description: The data domain where the quality issue was detected (e.g., Customer, Network, Billing, Product). Maps to the enterprise data domain taxonomy.

attributes.name: affected_product
attributes.description: The specific data product (table/entity) within the domain where the quality issue was identified.

attributes.name: affected_record_count
attributes.description: Number of data records impacted by this quality issue. Used to quantify the scope and business impact of the defect.

attributes.name: affected_report_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of business intelligence reports, dashboards, or analytics products impacted by this data quality issue for stakeholder notification.

attributes.name: business_impact_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the business consequences of this data quality issue including affected reports, analytics, operational processes, or regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: closed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the issue was verified as resolved and formally closed, completing the issue lifecycle.

attributes.name: compliance_impact_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this data quality issue affects regulatory reporting, compliance obligations, or audit requirements requiring special handling.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this DQ issue record was first created in the system for audit and lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: detected_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the data quality issue was first identified, marking the start of the issue lifecycle and SLA clock.

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: The method by which the data quality issue was discovered to support effectiveness analysis of detection mechanisms.

attributes.name: dq_dimension
attributes.description: The data quality dimension violated by this issue per ISO/IEC 25012 framework (e.g., completeness for missing values, accuracy for incorrect values).

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: Current escalation tier of the issue (0=no escalation, 1=team lead, 2=manager, 3=director, 4=executive) based on severity and SLA breach status.

attributes.name: estimated_revenue_impact
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact of the data quality issue on revenue recognition, billing accuracy, or revenue assurance in the base currency.

attributes.name: issue_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the data quality issue including symptoms, impact, and context discovered during DQ rule execution or manual review.

attributes.name: issue_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the DQ issue, formatted as DQI-YYYYMMDD for external reference and tracking.

attributes.name: issue_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the DQ issue tracking its progression from detection through remediation to closure.

attributes.name: issue_title
attributes.description: Short descriptive title summarizing the nature of the data quality issue for quick identification and reporting.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified the DQ issue record for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this DQ issue record was last updated, supporting audit trail and change history tracking.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Operational priority ranking for issue remediation combining severity, business impact, and resource availability. P1 requires immediate action.

attributes.name: recurrence_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this issue is a recurrence of a previously resolved issue, signaling potential systemic problems requiring deeper investigation.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action taken or planned to resolve the data quality issue including system fixes, data corrections, or process changes.

attributes.name: remediation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the remediation effort tracking progress from planning through implementation to verification.

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Detailed notes documenting the resolution approach, actions taken, validation results, and lessons learned for knowledge management.

attributes.name: resolved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the remediation action was completed and the issue was marked as resolved, stopping the SLA clock.

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the underlying cause of the data quality issue to support trend analysis and preventive action.

attributes.name: root_cause_detail
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of the root cause analysis findings including specific system, process, or configuration defect identified during investigation.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Business impact severity classification of the DQ issue determining prioritization and response urgency. Critical issues block downstream analytics or violate regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the issue resolution exceeded the SLA target time, triggering escalation and reporting requirements.

attributes.name: sla_target_resolution_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Resolution Hours
attributes.description: The number of hours within which this issue must be resolved per the data quality SLA based on severity level.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record where the defective data originated (e.g., Amdocs, Salesforce CRM, Nokia NetAct). Maps to the enterprise system catalog.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the system or user who created the DQ issue record for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: related_dq_issue_id

attributes.name: stretch_target_value

attributes.name: target_owner_role

attributes.name: target_period_end_date

attributes.name: target_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the measurement period for which this target is effective. Defines the beginning of the performance evaluation window.

attributes.name: target_period_type

products.name: ab_test

Captures experiment name, hypothesis, test type (A/B, multivariate, holdout), target population segment, treatment and control group definitions, primary success metric (KPI reference), secondary metrics, start date, end date, minimum detectable effect, statistical significance threshold, status (design, running, concluded, archived), and owning analytics team. Covers telecom experiments: pricing plan tests, network configuration trials, retention offer effectiveness, and UI/UX personalization tests.

attributes.name: analysis_method
attributes.description: The statistical method used to analyze experiment results, such as t-test, chi-square, ANOVA, Bayesian analysis, or regression.

attributes.name: business_sponsor
attributes.description: The business stakeholder or executive sponsor who requested the experiment and will act on the results.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_lower

attributes.name: confidence_interval_upper

attributes.name: data_source_system

attributes.name: decision_date

attributes.name: documentation_url

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: minimum_detectable_effect

attributes.name: modified_by

attributes.name: observed_effect_size
attributes.description: The actual measured effect size observed in the experiment, expressed as a percentage change or absolute difference in the primary metric.

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: The analytics or data science team responsible for designing, executing, and analyzing this experiment.

attributes.name: p_value
attributes.description: The calculated p-value from the statistical test, indicating the probability of observing the results under the null hypothesis.

attributes.name: planned_duration_days
attributes.description: The planned duration of the experiment in days, based on statistical power calculations and business requirements.

attributes.name: platform
attributes.description: The technology platform or tool used to execute the experiment, such as Optimizely, Adobe Target, or custom in-house platform.

attributes.name: primary_success_metric
attributes.description: The primary Key Performance Indicator (KPI) used to measure experiment success, such as ARPU (Average Revenue Per User), churn rate, NPS (Net Promoter Score), or conversion rate.

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the experiment has been reviewed and approved for compliance with applicable regulations such as FCC (Federal Communications Commission) rules, GDPR, or CPNI (Customer Proprietary Network Information) requirements.

attributes.name: result_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of the experiment results, including whether the hypothesis was supported, rejected, or inconclusive.

attributes.name: rollout_percentage

attributes.name: sample_size_control

attributes.name: sample_size_treatment
attributes.description: The number of subjects (customers, subscribers, or sessions) allocated to the treatment group(s).

attributes.name: statistical_significance_threshold
attributes.description: The p-value threshold used to determine statistical significance, typically 0.05 or 0.01, representing the acceptable Type I error rate.

attributes.name: test_code

attributes.name: test_name

attributes.description: The precise date and time when the subscriber or account was assigned to the experimental variant. Immutable once set to preserve experimental integrity and enable intent-to-treat analysis.

attributes.name: assignment_variant
attributes.description: The experimental variant or treatment group to which the subscriber or account has been assigned. Control represents the baseline, treatment groups represent experimental conditions, and holdout represents subjects excluded from exposure.

attributes.name: assignment_weight
attributes.description: Statistical weight applied to this assignment for weighted analysis. Used in inverse propensity weighting, stratification weighting, or other variance reduction techniques. Default value is 1.0 for equal weighting.

attributes.name: control_group_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this assignment is to the control group (True) or a treatment group (False). Simplifies filtering for control vs treatment comparisons.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this assignment record was first created in the system. Immutable audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this assignment record has passed all data quality validation rules. False indicates potential data quality issues that may warrant exclusion from analysis.

attributes.name: data_quality_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting any data quality issues, anomalies, or special conditions associated with this assignment. Used for audit trail and analysis exclusion decisions.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: The primary device type or Customer Premises Equipment (CPE) associated with the subscriber at the time of assignment. Examples include smartphone model, modem type, or set-top box model. Used for device-specific treatment effects analysis.

attributes.name: exclusion_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the subject was excluded or withdrawn from the experiment after initial assignment. Examples include account closure, service suspension, data quality issues, or violation of inclusion criteria.

attributes.name: exclusion_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the subject was excluded or withdrawn from the experiment. Used to calculate effective exposure duration.

attributes.name: experiment_end_date
attributes.description: The calendar date when the experiment period ends for this assignment. May be null for ongoing experiments. Used to define the analysis window and determine completion status.

attributes.name: experiment_start_date
attributes.description: The calendar date when the experiment period begins for this assignment. Used to define the analysis window and calculate time-in-experiment metrics.

attributes.name: exposure_confirmed_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the subject was actually exposed to the assigned treatment. True indicates confirmed exposure, False indicates assignment without exposure. Enables as-treated analysis in addition to intent-to-treat analysis.

attributes.name: exposure_count
attributes.description: The cumulative number of times the subject has been exposed to the treatment condition during the experiment period. Supports dose-response analysis.

attributes.name: first_exposure_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the subject was first exposed to the assigned treatment condition. May differ from assignment timestamp if there is a delay between assignment and actual exposure.

attributes.name: geographic_market
attributes.description: The geographic market, region, or service area in which the subscriber or account is located at the time of assignment. Used for geographic stratification and subgroup analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The user identifier or system process that last modified this assignment record. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this assignment record was last updated. Used to track changes to assignment status, exposure confirmation, or exclusion.

attributes.name: pre_experiment_arpu
attributes.description: The average monthly revenue per user for this subscriber or account in the period immediately preceding experiment assignment. Used as a covariate for difference-in-differences analysis and to verify randomization balance.

attributes.name: pre_experiment_churn_risk_score
attributes.description: The predicted churn probability (0.0000 to 1.0000) for this subscriber or account at the time of assignment, based on pre-experiment behavior. Used to verify balance across treatment arms and as a covariate in outcome analysis.

attributes.name: pre_experiment_tenure_months
attributes.description: The number of complete months the subscriber or account has been active with the telecommunications provider at the time of assignment. Used as a covariate to control for customer maturity effects.

attributes.name: propensity_score
attributes.description: The calculated propensity score (0.0000 to 1.0000) representing the predicted likelihood of treatment assignment based on pre-treatment covariates. Used in propensity score matching and weighting for causal inference.

attributes.name: rate_plan_code
attributes.description: The rate plan or pricing plan code associated with the subscriber or account at the time of assignment. Used to control for baseline pricing differences and analyze treatment effects by plan type.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: The primary telecommunications service type associated with the subscriber or account at the time of assignment. Used for service-specific subgroup analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mobile|fixed_broadband|fiber|iptv|voip|enterprise|converged — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: stratification_segment
attributes.description: The stratification segment or cohort to which the subject belongs for stratified randomization. Examples include ARPU tier, tenure band, geographic region, or device type to ensure balanced representation across key dimensions.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The user identifier or system process that created this assignment record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: reassigned_from_ab_test_assignment_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reassigned From Ab Test Assignment Id

products.name: retention_model_output
products.description: Operational output record of the subscriber churn and retention propensity model — the SSOT for model-scored subscriber retention risk in the Silver Layer. Captures subscriber reference, model run reference, scoring timestamp, churn propensity score (0.0–1.0), churn risk tier (low, medium, high, critical), predicted churn horizon (days), top contributing features (JSON), recommended retention action, and score expiry date. Consumed by the sales and customer domains for targeted retention campaign execution. Distinct from the analytical_model_registry which defines the model — this is the per-subscriber scored output record.
products.reference: TM Forum Churn Management — Predictive Analytics Output

attributes.name: coverage_area_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.cpe_asset. Business justification: CPE device type, age, condition are churn model features; linking predictions to assets enables targeted device upgrade offers as retention interventions.

attributes.name: model_run_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific model execution run that generated this score. Links to the analytical model run registry.

attributes.name: recent_trouble_ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to assurance.trouble_ticket. Business justification: Churn propensity scores consider recent trouble ticket history as a leading indicator. Real-world retention analytics incorporate service quality incidents into churn models for proactive retention in

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to analytics.segment_definition. Business justification: Retention model output includes subscriber segment classification. One output record belongs to ONE segment; one segment has MANY output records. Currently subscriber_segment is a string; normalizing

attributes.name: serving_ran_cell_id

attributes.name: subscriber_id
attributes.description: Reference to the subscriber who was scored by the retention model. Links to the customer domain subscriber entity.

attributes.name: arpu_at_scoring
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) at Scoring
attributes.description: The subscriber's monthly average revenue per user at the time of model scoring. Snapshot value used to prioritize high-value at-risk customers.

attributes.name: business_date
attributes.description: The business date (reporting date) for which this retention score is effective. Used for time-based partitioning and historical analysis.

attributes.name: churn_propensity_score
attributes.description: Predicted probability that the subscriber will churn within the forecast horizon. Continuous value between 0.0000 (no churn risk) and 1.0000 (certain churn). Core output of the retention model.

attributes.name: churn_risk_tier
attributes.description: Categorical segmentation of churn risk based on propensity score thresholds. Used for prioritizing retention campaigns and resource allocation.

attributes.name: cltv_at_scoring
attributes.description: The subscriber's estimated customer lifetime value at the time of model scoring. Snapshot value used to assess the business impact of potential churn.

attributes.name: competitive_offer_exposure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subscriber is in a geographic area with recent competitive promotional activity. True if exposed to competitor offers that may increase churn risk.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_lower
attributes.description: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for the churn propensity score. Represents the minimum likely churn probability given model uncertainty.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_upper
attributes.description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the churn propensity score. Represents the maximum likely churn probability given model uncertainty.

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: The date when the subscriber's current contract or commitment period ends. Critical for identifying churn risk windows and proactive retention timing.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this retention model output record was first created and persisted in the Silver Layer. Represents the data pipeline execution time.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The primary source system or platform that provided the input data for this model scoring (e.g., Salesforce CRM, Amdocs Billing, internal data lake).

attributes.name: days_to_contract_end
attributes.description: Number of days remaining until the subscriber's contract expires at the time of scoring. Key temporal feature for churn prediction near contract renewal periods.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Detailed error or warning message if the scoring process encountered issues for this subscriber. Null if processing completed successfully.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this retention model output record was last updated. Used for tracking record changes and data freshness.

attributes.name: model_drift_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether model drift was detected for this scoring run. True if input data distribution significantly differs from training data, suggesting potential score reliability issues.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the retention model that generated this score. Enables tracking of model evolution and performance comparison across versions.

attributes.name: nps_score
attributes.description: The subscriber's most recent Net Promoter Score rating (0-10 scale). Measures customer loyalty and likelihood to recommend the service.

attributes.name: predicted_churn_horizon_days
attributes.description: Number of days into the future for which the churn prediction is valid. Represents the forecast window of the model (e.g., 30, 60, 90 days).

attributes.name: previous_churn_score
attributes.description: The churn propensity score from the previous model run for this subscriber. Enables tracking of score changes and risk trajectory over time.

attributes.name: processing_status
attributes.description: Status of the scoring record processing. Completed indicates successful scoring; failed or partial indicates data quality or processing issues.

attributes.name: recent_complaint_count
attributes.description: Number of customer complaints or trouble tickets filed by the subscriber in the 90 days prior to scoring. Behavioral indicator of dissatisfaction and churn risk.

attributes.name: recent_payment_failure_count
attributes.description: Number of failed payment attempts in the 90 days prior to scoring. Financial indicator of potential involuntary churn risk.

attributes.name: recommended_retention_action
attributes.description: Model-recommended intervention strategy to reduce churn risk for this subscriber. Guides sales and customer success teams on next best action. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: no_action|monitor|outreach|discount_offer|loyalty_program|premium_support|contract_renegotiation — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: retention_campaign_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subscriber is eligible for proactive retention campaigns based on business rules (e.g., not recently contacted, not in dispute, contract status).

attributes.name: score_change_direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the churn risk has increased, decreased, or remained stable compared to the previous scoring cycle. New_score indicates first-time scoring for this subscriber.

attributes.name: score_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date after which this churn score is considered stale and should not be used for operational decisions. Calculated as scoring_timestamp plus model refresh interval.

attributes.name: score_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Assessment of the reliability and quality of this particular score based on feature completeness, data freshness, and model confidence. Low quality scores should be used with caution.

attributes.name: scoring_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the churn propensity score was calculated for this subscriber. Represents the business event time of model inference.

attributes.name: tenure_months_at_scoring
attributes.description: Number of months the subscriber has been active with the service provider at the time of scoring. Snapshot value used as a key churn predictor feature.

attributes.name: top_contributing_features
attributes.description: JSON-encoded list of the most influential features driving the churn prediction for this subscriber. Includes feature names and their contribution weights for model explainability.

attributes.name: usage_trend
attributes.description: Directional trend of the subscriber's service usage over the past 90 days. Declining usage is a strong churn predictor.

attributes.name: previous_retention_model_output_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on retention_model_output (previous_retention_model_output_id)

attributes.name: service_availability_flag

attributes.name: service_territory_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the service territory, including geographic landmarks, boundary definitions, operational notes, and any special characteristics or constraints.

attributes.name: site_count
attributes.description: Total number of network sites, cell towers, Points of Presence (POP), or infrastructure facilities located within the service territory boundaries.
attributes.references: TM Forum SID - Resource Inventory ABE

attributes.name: sla_response_time_minutes

attributes.name: territory_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the service territory, used across operational systems for territory reference and assignment.

attributes.name: territory_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the service territory, typically reflecting geographic or organizational designation (e.g., 'Northeast Metro Region', 'Downtown Dispatch Zone').
attributes.references: TM Forum SID - Geographic Address ABE

attributes.name: territory_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the service territory: active (in operational use), inactive (temporarily not in use), proposed (planned but not yet activated), suspended (temporarily disabled), retired (permanently decommissioned).

attributes.name: territory_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service territory by operational purpose: field_ops (field operations coverage), sales_region (sales team assignment), noc_zone (Network Operations Center monitoring zone), dispatch_zone (workforce dispatch area), franchise_area (licensed service area), regulatory_zone (compliance jurisdiction).
attributes.references: TM Forum eTOM - Resource Management and Operations

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the service territory (e.g., 'America/New_York'), used for scheduling, Service Level Agreement (SLA) calculations, and workforce dispatch timing.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the service territory record, incremented with each modification to support change history and optimistic locking.

attributes.name: parent_service_territory_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on service_territory (parent_service_territory_id)

products.name: exchange
products.description: Master record for telecommunications exchange facilities — telephone exchanges, DSLAMs, street cabinets (RIMs/FTTCs), and GPON headend points that define the logical service delivery boundary for fixed-line broadband and voice services. Captures exchange identifier, exchange name, exchange code (Telstra/BT/AT&T exchange code), exchange type (main_exchange, remote_integrated_multiplexer, street_cabinet, GPON_headend), operator, address reference, geo-coordinates, technology served (ADSL2+, VDSL2, FTTC, FTTN, FTTP, HFC), maximum serviceable premises count, current connected premises count, exchange status (operational, planned, decommissioned), commissioning date, and regulatory reporting flag. Critical for service qualification and NBN/FTTP rollout planning.
products.reference: TM Forum SID Network Location / NBN Co Exchange Registry / BT Openreach Exchange

attributes.name: exchange_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the telecommunications exchange facility. Primary key.

attributes.name: location_address_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical address record where the exchange facility is located. Links to the address master data product.

attributes.name: primary_network_element_id

attributes.name: annual_opex
attributes.description: Estimated annual Operational Expenditure (OPEX) for maintaining and operating this exchange facility, including power, maintenance, and support costs. Used for profitability analysis and budget planning.

attributes.name: asset_tag
attributes.description: Physical asset tag or serial number affixed to the exchange equipment for inventory tracking and asset management. Links to the enterprise asset management system.

attributes.name: available_ports
attributes.description: Number of ports currently available for new customer connections. Calculated as port_capacity minus currently allocated ports. Used for real-time service qualification.

attributes.name: backbone_connection_type
attributes.description: Type of backhaul or backbone connectivity linking this exchange to the core network. Determines reliability, latency, and bandwidth capabilities.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the exchange facility was officially commissioned and made operational for service delivery. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and depreciation calculations.

attributes.name: coverage_radius_km
attributes.description: Approximate service coverage radius from the exchange facility in kilometers. Represents the maximum distance at which acceptable service quality can be maintained for the primary technology served.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this exchange record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and record lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: TM Forum SID - Common Business Entities

attributes.name: current_connected_premises
attributes.description: Number of premises currently connected and receiving active service from this exchange. Used to calculate utilization rate and available capacity.

attributes.name: data_source_system

attributes.name: decommissioning_date

attributes.name: environmental_zone
attributes.description: Classification of the geographic environment where the exchange is located. Used for network planning, service pricing, and regulatory reporting of rural broadband coverage.

attributes.name: equipment_model
attributes.description: Model number or designation of the primary exchange equipment installed at this facility. Used for technical support, firmware updates, and capacity planning.

attributes.name: exchange_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the exchange facility, typically reflecting the geographic area or locality served (e.g., 'Downtown Central Exchange', 'Suburban North DSLAM').

attributes.name: exchange_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the exchange facility. Determines service availability and eligibility for new customer connections.

attributes.name: exchange_type
attributes.description: Classification of the exchange facility based on its function in the network topology. Determines the service delivery model and technology capabilities.

attributes.name: firmware_version
attributes.description: Current firmware or software version running on the exchange equipment. Critical for security patch management, feature availability, and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: installation_cost
attributes.description: Total Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) incurred for the initial installation and commissioning of the exchange facility. Used for Return on Investment (ROI) analysis and asset valuation.

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent scheduled maintenance activity performed on the exchange facility. Used for preventive maintenance scheduling and Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) analysis.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this exchange record was last modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit compliance.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the exchange facility in decimal degrees format. Used for network planning, coverage mapping, and service qualification.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the exchange facility in decimal degrees format. Used for network planning, coverage mapping, and service qualification.

attributes.name: max_serviceable_premises
attributes.description: Total number of residential and business premises that can theoretically be served from this exchange based on its capacity and coverage footprint. Used for network capacity planning and market sizing.

attributes.name: mttr_target_hours
attributes.description: Target Mean Time to Repair in hours for this exchange facility as defined in the Service Level Agreement (SLA). Represents the maximum acceptable downtime for fault resolution.

attributes.name: nbn_rollout_flag

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next preventive maintenance activity on the exchange facility. Used for workforce planning and customer communication regarding potential service interruptions.

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Name of the telecommunications operator or service provider that owns and operates this exchange facility.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Ownership model for the exchange facility. Determines Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) vs Operational Expenditure (OPEX) treatment, maintenance responsibilities, and asset depreciation.

attributes.name: port_capacity
attributes.description: Total number of physical or logical ports available at this exchange for customer connections. Represents the hard capacity limit for simultaneous active services.

attributes.name: power_backup_type
attributes.description: Type of backup power system installed at the exchange facility to ensure service continuity during power outages. Critical for Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance and disaster recovery planning.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exchange facility must be included in regulatory reporting submissions to governing bodies (FCC, Ofcom, etc.). True if the exchange serves a regulated service area or meets reporting thresholds.

attributes.name: service_territory_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the administrative service territory or franchise area that this exchange serves. Used for regulatory compliance, billing zone determination, and market segmentation.

attributes.name: sla_tier
attributes.description: Service level tier assigned to this exchange facility, determining restoration time commitments, monitoring frequency, and support priority. Higher tiers serve business-critical or high-revenue areas.

attributes.name: technology_served
attributes.description: Primary broadband access technology delivered from this exchange facility. Determines service speed capabilities and customer eligibility for specific product offerings.

attributes.name: vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the equipment vendor or manufacturer that supplied the primary exchange infrastructure (e.g., Nokia, Ericsson, Huawei, Cisco). Used for maintenance planning, spare parts management, and vendor performance tracking.

attributes.name: wholesale_access_flag

products.name: premise

Captures premise identifier, premise type (residential_single, residential_apartment, commercial_small, commercial_large, MDU, government, industrial), address reference, geo-coordinates, building name, floor number, unit number, MDU parent premise reference, serviceable flag per technology (FTTP_serviceable, HFC_serviceable, FTTN_serviceable, FWA_serviceable, 5G_serviceable), premise status (active, demolished, under_construction), lot/parcel number, cadastral reference, and last survey date. The SSOT for premises distinct from customer.address which is customer-centric.

attributes.name: premise_id

attributes.name: broadband_serviceable_location_premise_id

attributes.name: dslam_element_id

attributes.name: mdu_parent_premise_id

attributes.name: business_count

attributes.name: hfc_serviceable_flag

attributes.name: last_survey_date

attributes.name: latitude

attributes.name: longitude

attributes.name: lot_number
attributes.description: Legal lot or parcel number assigned by local government for property identification and taxation purposes.

attributes.name: n5g_serviceable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the premise is within 5G New Radio (5G NR) coverage area and can receive 5G mobile services. True if 5G coverage exists, false otherwise.

products.name: address_validation_event

attributes.name: address_validation_event_id

attributes.name: primary_address_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user or automated process that triggered the address validation event. May be a user ID for manual validations or a system process identifier for automated batch validations.

attributes.name: api_response_code
attributes.description: The HTTP or service-specific response code returned by the validation API. Captures technical success or error codes from the external geocoding service (e.g., 200 for success, 400 for bad request, 500 for service error).

attributes.name: api_response_message
attributes.description: Detailed message or description returned by the validation API. Provides additional context about the validation result, including error messages, warnings, or informational notes from the geocoding service.

attributes.description: The standardized city or locality name returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to match official postal authority city names.

attributes.description: The standardized three-letter country code returned by the validation service. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format (e.g., USA, GBR, AUS, CAN).

attributes.name: corrected_postal_code
attributes.description: The standardized postal code or ZIP code returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to match authoritative postal code format and assignment.

attributes.name: corrected_state_province
attributes.description: The standardized state, province, or region code returned by the validation service. Typically uses official postal abbreviations (e.g., CA for California, NSW for New South Wales).

attributes.description: The standardized street name component returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to the input street name including spelling, abbreviations, and directional prefixes.

attributes.description: The standardized street number component returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to the input street number to match authoritative format.

attributes.description: The standardized street type component (e.g., Street, Avenue, Road, Boulevard) returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to match postal authority standards.

attributes.name: corrected_unit_number
attributes.description: The standardized unit, apartment, or suite number component returned by the validation service. Captures any corrections made to secondary address designators.

attributes.description: System timestamp when this address validation event record was first created in the data platform. Audit field for data lineage and record lifecycle tracking in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.description: USPS-specific indicator confirming whether the address is a valid delivery point. Y indicates confirmed deliverable address; N indicates not confirmed; S indicates address is missing secondary (unit) number; D indicates address matched to USPS database but missing secondary information. Critical for mail deliverability assessment.

attributes.name: geocoding_accuracy_level
attributes.description: Precision level of the geocoding result. Rooftop indicates exact building location; parcel indicates property boundary; street indicates street segment; intersection indicates cross-street; postal_code indicates ZIP/postcode centroid; city, region, country indicate progressively coarser granularity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rooftop|parcel|street|intersection|postal_code|city|region|country — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: geocoding_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate returned by the geocoding service, expressed in decimal degrees. Represents the north-south position of the validated address on Earth's surface, ranging from -90 to +90 degrees.

attributes.name: geocoding_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate returned by the geocoding service, expressed in decimal degrees. Represents the east-west position of the validated address on Earth's surface, ranging from -180 to +180 degrees.

attributes.name: input_address_string
attributes.description: The raw, unvalidated address string submitted for validation. Captures the exact input as received from the user or system before any normalization or correction.

attributes.name: match_confidence_score
attributes.description: Numerical confidence score indicating the quality of the address match, ranging from 0 to 100. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in the validation result. Score of 100 represents exact match, lower scores indicate partial or interpolated matches.

attributes.name: match_type
attributes.description: Classification of the address match result. Exact indicates perfect match to authoritative database; partial indicates some components matched; interpolated indicates address was estimated based on range; no_match indicates validation failed; ambiguous indicates multiple possible matches; corrected indicates input was modified to match standard.

attributes.name: matched_address_string
attributes.description: The standardized, validated address string returned by the validation service. Represents the best match found in the authoritative address database.

attributes.name: residential_delivery_indicator
attributes.description: Classification indicating whether the validated address is a residential or commercial location. Used for service eligibility determination, pricing, and network planning decisions in telecommunications service delivery.

attributes.name: validation_cost_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO currency code for the validation cost amount. Typically USD for most geocoding API services.

attributes.name: validation_duration_ms
attributes.description: Time taken to complete the address validation request, measured in milliseconds. Used for performance monitoring and Service Level Agreement (SLA) tracking of validation service response times.

attributes.name: validation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing additional context, observations, or special handling instructions related to the validation event. May include manual review notes, data quality observations, or business rules applied during validation.

attributes.name: validation_source

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Overall status of the address validation event. attributes.name: validation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the address validation event was performed. Captures the precise moment of validation execution in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Captures version identifier, coverage area reference, version number, version effective date, version expiry date, geometry snapshot (WKT polygon), technology type, coverage tier, predicted signal strength, predicted throughput, change reason (network_expansion, cell_reconfig, decommission, model_update, drive_test_correction), changed by (system or operator), and approval status. attributes.name: premises_covered

attributes.name: version_notes

attributes.name: premises_passed_id

attributes.name: network_rollout_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the network rollout zone or deployment area within which this premise was passed. Used for tracking infrastructure expansion by geographic deployment phases.

attributes.name: activation_readiness_status
attributes.description: Current status of the premises readiness for service activation. attributes.name: business_premise_flag

attributes.name: connection_cost_tier

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: data_source

attributes.name: distance_to_network_metres

attributes.name: estimated_connection_cost

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: maximum_service_speed_mbps

attributes.name: pass_reference_number

attributes.name: priority_level

attributes.name: qos_class

attributes.name: record_status
